transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi. I came in today because I just can’t seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It honestly feels like everything I built up after my divorce has just collapsed, and I’m just... sitting under it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about a month now. It just started hanging over me right around the time all the... the financial mess from the divorce really hit.
Have you been feeling down or hopeless nearly every day since this started, or have there been significant periods where you felt better?

It's been every day. Like I mentioned, I just... I really can't shake that heavy feeling at all. There haven't been any breaks or days where I felt better. It just constantly feels like I'm sitting under the weight of everything collapsing, and it doesn't let up.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with others?

No, not really. I mean, I still care about my work and... and the things I usually do. I still want to see my friends. It's just that I feel so weighed down while I'm doing those things. But the actual interest in them hasn't gone away. So, no, I haven't really noticed a loss of interest or anything like that.
Have you been feeling fatigued or experiencing a lack of energy almost every day?

Yes, definitely. Getting through a normal workday right now... it just feels like I'm dragging myself through wet concrete. I'm exhausted all the time. Even just doing basic things, like taking a shower or just opening my laptop to start work, it takes way more energy than I actually have. It's an effort just to keep moving.
Would you say that your mood has been persistently low or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, over this past month?

Yes, definitely. That's actually why I came in. I just can't shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It's like... like everything I've built since my divorce has just collapsed, and I'm just sitting underneath all of it. It's been like that most of the day, pretty much every single day.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? Like a significant decrease in how much you're eating or unintentional weight loss?
No, not really. My appetite has been pretty normal, I think. I haven't noticed any weight loss or... or eating less than usual. I still manage to eat my regular meals, so no, no real changes there.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty, like you’re a burden or that you’ve failed in some way, nearly every day during this time?

Yes, absolutely. It's... it's pretty constant. I just keep telling myself that I'm a terrible engineer, that I'm a failed wife. I really feel like a burden to everyone around me. I find myself just replaying every little missed calculation at work or... or any tense email I've sent, and I just look at it like it's proof that I ruin everything I touch. It's just this overwhelming feeling of guilt and worthlessness every day.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life during this time?

Yes, I have. Um... I’ve just been thinking a lot that it would be easier if I didn’t wake up. The thoughts... they got intense enough recently that I actually scared myself. That's when I realized I needed to do something, so I called the employee assistance program at work.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one where you felt this same kind of hopelessness or depression?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone, but... nothing like this. This heavy, constant feeling of being worthless and just wanting it to stop... this is the first time it's ever been this bad.
Have you ever had a period of feeling down or hopeless that was noticeable but didn’t last as long or wasn’t quite this severe?

No, I really haven't. Um, like I said, I've had normal stressful weeks at work or just regular bad days, but... no periods where I felt hopeless or noticeably down like you're describing. This whole experience is really new to me.
Before this current episode, have you ever had a time when you felt down or hopeless for several days or more, even if it wasn't as severe or long-lasting as what you're experiencing now?

No, really, I haven't. I know you're trying to see if there's a pattern, but... there just isn't. Like I said, I've had normal stress, but never a string of days where I felt depressed or hopeless before this. This is definitely the first time.

Before this current episode, have you ever experienced a time when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for more than just a day or two, even if it wasn’t as severe as what you're going through now?

No, I... I really haven't. I'm sorry, I feel like I keep giving you the same answer, but it's just the truth. I've never lost interest in things or felt hopeless for days at a time before this started. This is... this is all completely new territory for me.
Have you ever had an episode of depression before this one that lasted for several weeks or more, even if it was separated by a period of feeling better for two months or more?

No, I haven't. I know you're asking about longer timeframes now, like several weeks, but my answer is still no. I've never dealt with anything like this in the past, whether it was for a few days or a few weeks. This current time is the very first time I've ever felt this way.

Have you ever had a period of time lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things, followed by a period of at least two months where you felt completely back to normal before this current episode began?

I know you're trying to be really specific with the timelines now, like two weeks of feeling down and two months of feeling normal, but... no. I really haven't. Like I've been saying, I never experienced any kind of depression or hopelessness before this current situation started. I was just living my normal life, working, doing my usual things. So, no, nothing like that has ever happened to me in the past.
Before this current episode, have you ever had a major depressive episode that lasted for at least two weeks, followed by a period of at least two months where you felt completely back to normal?

I... I think we're going in circles a bit here. No, I haven't. Like I said, I have never had a major depressive episode before now. Not for two weeks, not ever. Before this current situation, I was just completely normal all the time. I've never been through anything like this before.
